problems.title: Copy List with Random Pointer

gfg.t: Clone List with Next and Random

problems.gist: You get the head of a singly linked list of n nodes. Each node has an integer val, a next pointer and a random pointer that is either null or points to some node of this same list.

problems.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
problems.gist: You get the head of a singly linked list and a positive integer k. Split the list, from the front, into consecutive groups of exactly k nodes, reverse the order of the nodes inside every complete group, and return the head of the resulting list.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.gist: You get head, the first node of a singly linked list (each node has an integer val and a next pointer; the last node's next is null).

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List

gfg.t: Kth from End of Linked List

problems.gist: You get the head of a singly linked list and an integer n. Delete the node that is n-th from the end of the list (n = 1 is the last node, n = length is the first node) and return the head of the resulting list. If the list had one node and you delete it, return null.

problems.title: Add Two Numbers
problems.gist: Two non-negative integers are given as non-empty singly linked lists, one decimal digit per node, with the digits stored in reverse order (the head holds the ones digit). Return their sum as a linked list in the same reverse-digit format.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.gist: You get the heads of two singly linked lists, list1 and list2. Each list is sorted in non-decreasing order (equal values may repeat). Build one sorted list by splicing together the existing nodes of the two lists, and return its head.

problems.title: Find the Duplicate Number
problems.gist: You get an integer array nums of length n + 1. Every value lies in the range [1, n]. Exactly one value is repeated (it may appear two or more times); every other value appears at most once. Return the repeated value.

problems.title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
problems.gist: You get the heads of two singly linked lists, headA and headB. Return the first node that both lists share (the same node object, by identity), or null if the lists never meet. After a shared node, both lists continue through the same nodes to the end.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.gist: You get head, the first node of a singly linked list. Return true if the list contains a cycle: some node can be reached again by following next pointers. Otherwise return false.

problems.title: Palindrome Linked List
problems.gist: You get the head of a singly linked list of digits. Return true if the values read the same from front to back and from back to front, and false otherwise.

problems.title: Sort List
problems.gist: You are given the head of a singly linked list of integers. Rearrange the list so that its values appear in non-decreasing order and return the head of the sorted list. You may relink the existing nodes (the usual approach) rather than allocate new ones.

problems.title: Happy Number
problems.gist: Decide whether a positive integer n is happy. Starting from n, repeatedly replace the current number with the sum of the squares of its decimal digits. If this process eventually reaches 1 (where it stays, because 1² = 1), n is happy.

problems.title: Rotate List
problems.gist: You get the head of a singly linked list and a non-negative integer k. Rotate the list to the right by k places: one rotation moves the last node to the front. Return the head of the rotated list.
